facts.raw_span: A 31-year-old male nursing student
history of axillary hyperhidrosis
excessive sweating of the buttocks, most severe at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum
previously treated his axillary condition successfully with 20% aluminum chloride
treatment of the intergluteal cleft and sacrum with aluminum chloride was unsuccessful
used absorbent pads yet continued to soak through his pants
consequently unable to attend work
Minor starch-iodine test was performed
Areas of significant sweating were identified in the sacral region (10 × 3-cm area) and intergluteal cleft (6 × 8-cm area)
a 10 × 3-cm grid was drawn on the sacrum and a 6 × 8-cm grid was drawn on the intergluteal cleft
with the outermost dots omitted

support_spans: excessive sweating of the buttocks, most severe at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum
Areas of significant sweating were identified in the sacral region (10 × 3-cm area) and intergluteal cleft (6 × 8-cm area)
concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of excessive sweating in specific areas, confirmed by the Minor starch-iodine test, support the diagnosis of Focal Hyperhidrosis.

support_spans: previously treated his axillary condition successfully with 20% aluminum chloride
contradict_spans: treatment of the intergluteal cleft and sacrum with aluminum chloride was unsuccessful
concepts.why: The patient's history of axillary hyperhidrosis and successful treatment with aluminum chloride suggest Primary Hyperhidrosis, but the lack of response to treatment in the intergluteal cleft and sacrum areas may indicate a different or additional condition.
It explains the excessive sweating in specific areas such as the sacrum and intergluteal cleft.

rationales.F02: History of axillary hyperhidrosis suggests a possible diagnosis of primary hyperhidrosis.
rationales.F03: Excessive sweating of the buttocks, most severe at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum, is a strong indicator of focal hyperhidrosis.
rationales.F05: Unsuccessful treatment of the intergluteal cleft and sacrum with aluminum chloride may indicate a more severe or resistant form of hyperhidrosis.
rationales.F08: The Minor starch-iodine test was performed to localize areas of excessive sweating, which is a common diagnostic procedure for hyperhidrosis.
rationales.F09: Identification of significant sweating areas in the sacral region and intergluteal cleft supports a diagnosis of focal hyperhidrosis.

frontier_selector.why: The evidence of excessive sweating localized to specific areas such as the intergluteal cleft and sacrum, as identified by the Minor starch-iodine test, decided it.
